newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Juppe confirms to cut VAT, no timing yet.
newsitem.headline: France's Juppe confirms to cut VAT, no timing yet.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe reaffirmed on Friday his promise to cut France's value added tax (VAT), pledging to bring it down to about 17 or 18 percent from its current level of 20.6 percent.
He gave no timeframe for the cut, which was promised when the centre-right government raised the VAT in the summer of 1995.
"We will have to bring the TVA back towards the European average around 17 to 18 percent," Juppe said in an interview with daily Le Parisien.
Juppe said the tax increase was necessary in 1995 to help cut France's accumulated deficits but he admitted that move had a bad effect on consumer psychology.
"I admit that the increase had psychological effects. And since economics is also about psychology..." the paper quoted him as saying.
